collection.description: A villager has added one stone a day to a pile on the beach for years, and someone finally asks why.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Years ago (subject) put a stone on a flat spot at the edge of the beach, for no reason at all. The next day (subject.he/she) put another one on top. (subject.He/She) has added one stone almost every day since. The pile is now taller than most children, and today (friend) stops beside it and asks the question (subject) has been dreading: "Why?"

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (subject) opens (subject.his/her) mouth. Closes it. Tries again. "It was one stone," (subject.he/she) says at last, "and then it would have been rude to stop." (friend) considers the pile for a long moment, then picks up a small stone and holds it out. "May I?" (subject) thinks about it. "Just this once."

b.name: Answer B
b.text: "No reason," says (subject), and puts today's stone on top. (friend) waits for more. There is no more. (friend) walks on, shaking (friend.his/her) head, and (subject) stands back to admire the pile. It is, (subject.he/she) thinks, a very good pile.
